title: CastillosCVEP100
description: EEG recordings from 12 healthy participants performing an offline 4-class code-modulated visual evoked potential (c-VEP) brain-computer interface task. The study compares burst c-VEP and m-sequence stimulation at 100% and 40% amplitude depth, evaluating classification accuracy with a CNN decoder as well as subjective visual comfort. Data were recorded with a 32-channel BrainProducts LiveAmp system at 500 Hz and are distributed in BIDS format via MOABB.
methods_description: Factorial design with four conditions (burst or m-sequence code, each at 100% or 40% amplitude depth). Participants attended to four cued targets over 15 blocks of 4 trials per condition, with a 0.5 s cue, 2.2 s stimulation and 0.7 s inter-trial period. EEG was recorded from 32 active electrodes (BrainProducts LiveAmp, 500 Hz), and decoding used a CNN on 250 ms sliding windows. Subjective ratings of comfort, tiredness and intrusiveness were also collected.
